title: Synthflow Pricing 2026 for 1K, 10K & 100K Minutes
summary: Synthflow pricing includes self-serve tiers with bundled minutes, plus overage and concurrency charges.
body_markdown:
## The business case for Synthflow


If you pay for Synthflow, the best argument is the engineering time it saves. A month billed at an unfamiliar overage rate is still cheaper than the engineering weeks you would spend avoiding it, provided those weeks are scarce.


### Why Synthflow's higher price can be worth it


Start with who gets paged. In a hand-built voice agent, the person who wrote the telephony glue, the speech handling and the retry logic is the person woken when a call drops at 2am on a Tuesday.


If that person is a contractor who has since left, nobody owns the failure.


With a no-code builder, part of that ownership moves to the vendor, and a non-engineer can change a script without a deployment.


That's the real saving, and it's larger than the build time alone. A working agent in an afternoon means a team can test whether callers will talk to it at all before committing a developer to it.


If the answer is no, the platform fee was the price of finding out cheaply.


That's the case for a business with no spare engineers, or one that needs a pilot live this month.


### Where Synthflow pricing stops paying off at volume


It only holds while the premium stays small next to the labor it replaces. That stops being true as volume rises.


**You pay engineering cost once** ; the all-in minute, with overage, telephony and add-ons counted, is paid on every call, indefinitely. At high volume the gap between that minute and an API-first rival's compounds each month, and a developer's build time is repaid quickly.


> You pay engineering cost once; the all-in minute, with overage, telephony and add-ons counted, is paid on every call, indefinitely.


When a developer is already on staff, the no-code advantage also shrinks. Their time to a first working agent is longer, but it is a one-off, and they leave you with code your team owns and can move between vendors.


The glue around the call is the one part you can buy cheaply either way.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can start the Synthflow call from a CRM event and write the result back to the record, and the run is the meter, not the steps inside it: a flow costs 1 credit whether it has two steps or ten, which means your costs don't scale with workflow complexity, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module.


Splitting the work into smaller, safer steps therefore never raises the bill. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production. That prices only the plumbing; the all-in minute stays Synthflow's.


It comes down to one condition: whether you have a developer available and the call volume to justify using them. If you have neither, pay for speed. If you have both, build, and price the minute before you sign.
